verdict.rationale: GitBook documents a block-based visual web editor with real-time collaboration and built-in Git workflows, plus GitHub/GitLab Sync. Its docs state you can 'write in the editor... or sync from Git', so web edits and repo content share one source of truth. A community user independently praises the web-based editor, and change requests support review of teammates' edits. Missing for 10: explicit evidence that Git Sync is bidirectional and how conflicts are handled, and independent hands-on corroboration of the editor-to-Git round trip.
